concepts.title: Agent Deck

concepts.bestFor: A memorable, tactile home screen and fast agent switching.
concepts.tradeoff: Tiny key displays are for recognition, not reading; detail opens in the main viewer.

concepts.title: Screen Wall
concepts.interaction: Arrange agent workspaces as resizable screen tiles. Enlarge one with a click, pin two for comparison, and leave idle agents as compact cards.
concepts.bestFor: Watching browser research, visual work and parallel tasks.
concepts.tradeoff: A wall of continuously refreshed screens can become distracting and expensive; only active or focused tiles need live updates.

concepts.title: Shared Workbench
concepts.interaction: Put the current artifact at the center. Ask an agent to work on a selected paragraph, file or browser page; review its proposal beside the original.
concepts.bestFor: Producing and reviewing documents, code and designs with less window switching.
concepts.tradeoff: Best for focused work; weaker than a screen wall for monitoring many tasks.

concepts.tradeoff: Less ambient visibility; a live-agent drawer provides optional inspection.

concepts.title: Agent Mixer
concepts.interaction: Give each agent a control strip with its task, screen, queue priority and explicit pause control. Bring a selected agent into the main viewer while retaining an overview of the team.
concepts.bestFor: People who like direct controls and frequent switching between agents.
concepts.tradeoff: Controls must have precise meanings; priority would order queued work, not make a model think faster.
